## Glossary

**archive connect**  
Verify access and save a destination (alias `setup`); does not upload.

**archive sync --dry-run**  
Prints per destination the ids cleanup would delete; publishes nothing.

**backoff**  
30 s doubling to 30 min; per archive per destination for a refusal, whole destination for an outage.

**checked**  
A plan every window of which passed the sensitivity pass; only its parts publish.

**cleanup**  
Top-level destinations.json key: off (default) | leaked | all; whether sync deletes at destinations.

**cleanupFor**  
Per-organization cleanup overrides; also the function reading the effective mode.

**destination**  
A top-level `destinations` entry naming its `organizationId`: a direct Archive or a Kingdom library.

**destinations**  
Class: destination config: direct Archive and Kingdom destinations, connect/remove, token files, remote search.

**DPoP**  
Proof-of-possession signature sent fresh with each Kingdom call; @inixiative/signet renews the token.

**Installation**  
This Archive registered with Kingdom, named by a key under `<home>/config/kingdom/<host>/`.

**Kingdom**  
The permission hub; keeps no archive store and forwards writes to the hosted Archive.

**kingdom-pairing**  
Class: pairing with Kingdom: pairWithKingdom, held Signets, paired libraries, kingdomArchiveOperation.

**leaked**  
A whole-session copy at a destination; `leaked` mode deletes it unless reviewed and routed whole while publish is off.

**library**  
A hosted Archive resource in Kingdom; pairing asks sessions.write and sessions.delete on it.

**outbox**  
A queued revision awaiting delivery to a destination.

**pending**  
A tombstone's destination deletes still awaiting confirmation; stay queued while cleanup is off.

**receipt**  
The digest a destination last acknowledged for an archive.

**remote-deletion**  
Class: deleting at destinations: re-plan deletes, leaked whole copies, cleanup/cleanupFor, tombstone-queued deletes, deleteRemote.

**restore**  
Flag on a re-routed part so a direct destination lifts its tombstone; Kingdom has no restore.

**routingPreview**  
Backs `archive routes`: where each archive routes; sends nothing, reports no deletes.

**serve --sync**  
The server mode that runs syncArchives every 30 seconds.

**Signet**  
The credential `archive pair` collects (0600); every call carries its token and a DPoP proof.

**sourceId**  
This Archive's id; Kingdom accepts only its own, and cleanup never touches another's copies.

**sync-publish**  
Class: the sync loop: syncArchives, publishArchive, receipts and outbox, backoff, routes preview.

**tokenFile / tokenEnv**  
Where a direct destination's token lives; private file (chmod 600, no symlink) or env var name, never the token.

## 1. What this Warden covers

Destinations and delivery: the direct and Kingdom destinations an organization publishes to, the sync loop that delivers parts with receipts, an outbox and backoff, the cleanup modes that govern deletes at destinations, and pairing with Kingdom to reach hosted Archives with a Signet.

## 2. The domain

A destination is an entry of the top-level `destinations` array of destinations.json carrying its `organizationId`: a direct Archive (URL plus a private tokenFile or tokenEnv; the token is never stored, read on every request, HTTPS or loopback HTTP only, redirects refused) or a Kingdom library reached with a paired Signet (archiveDestinationSchema accepts both; kingdomDestinationSchema only the latter). Add one with `archive connect` or connectDestination, remove one with removeDestination, show one with describeDestination (never the raw entry). Over HTTP, destinations/connect and destinations/remove take Kingdom routes through an already-paired Signet only, and exist only when the server has config.

syncArchives (`@inixiative/archive/client`) is the whole pass: `serve --sync` runs it every 30 seconds and `archive sync` asks the server for one; it publishes only parts of checked plans, and only while `publish` is on. publishArchive sends one archive to one destination; archiveRequest and kingdomArchiveOperation are the per-call transports it picks between. routingPreview backs `archive routes`, sends nothing and reports no deletes; `archive sync --dry-run` publishes nothing and reports only what sync would delete. A refusal backs off that archive at that destination (retried at once on a new revision); only an outage (no answer or 5xx) pauses the whole destination.

Deletes at a destination (re-plans, deletions, retention, tombstones' pending deletes, leaked whole copies) run only when that organization's cleanup (cleanupFor, set with setCleanup or `archive cleanup`) is `leaked` or `all`; off is the default and pending deletes stay queued. `leaked` keeps a whole copy routed whole only while publish is off. deleteRemote removes one copy. Kingdom: `archive pair` (pairWithKingdom, internal) registers an Installation and collects a Signet; writes go through `POST /api/v1/access/execute` with DPoP. Not here: which organizations a part names and the publish switch (routing-organizations); planning parts (routing-planning); the server's own HTTP API and CLI wiring (running-the-archive); receipts and outbox tables (session-store); local deletion, retention and tombstones (what-an-archive-keeps).

**Source:** `README.md` § Connect to BYO hosting (in "Archive")

#### Connect to BYO hosting

Every deployment runs the published image `ghcr.io/inixiative/archive` (tags: version, `latest`, commit SHA), built from main for amd64 and arm64, with `DATABASE_URL` pointing at Postgres 15 or later with pgvector, HTTPS in front, and a unique `ARCHIVE_SERVER_TOKEN` of at least 32 characters. It needs nothing else. The Render blueprint provisions the database, the image and a generated token together. On Railway, add a pgvector Postgres service and the image as a service with `DATABASE_URL` referencing it (`railway.json` builds the Dockerfile when deploying from the repository instead).

The local Archive publishes onward to destinations. Place the destination's token in a private file under the server's config directory (`chmod 600`, owned by you) or an environment variable, then run:

```sh
archive organizations set --id inixiative --project inixiative --project template --project kingdom
archive connect --url https://your-archive.example --organization-id inixiative --token-file ~/.local/share/archive/config/credentials/inixiative.token
archive search --remote --query 'migration'
```

`setup` is an alias for `connect`. Setup verifies access before saving `<home>/config/destinations.json` and does not upload; the Compose server (`serve --sync`) reads it and publishes every 30 seconds. `sync` and `routes` ask that server to run the same publication, or preview it, once. The URL locates the server; the token grants access. Configuration stores only the token file path (`tokenFile`) or environment variable name (`--token-env`, `tokenEnv`), never the token. A token file is read on every request, so rotating it needs no restart; symlinks and files readable by group or others are refused. Redirects are refused; only HTTPS or loopback HTTP is allowed.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#routing/routing-over-http -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Routing › Routing over HTTP (in "Archive")

##### Routing over HTTP

The server manages routes over HTTP too, so Foundry can read and set them. Only Kingdom destinations are set this way, through the Signets `pair` collected; direct token destinations stay CLI-only.

| Action | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `destinations/list` | `organizationId?` | `destinations`: each as `connect` reports it, with `delivered` (the organization's archives acknowledged at their latest digest) and `pending` |
| `organizations/list` | none | `organizations`: each `id` and its `projects` |
| `organizations/set` | `id`, `projects` | `organizations` |
| `organizations/remove` | `id` | `removed` |
| `destinations/libraries` | none | `paired`, and the `libraries` (`integrationId`, `resourceId`, `name`) the held Signets may write to |
| `destinations/connect` | `organizationId`, `integrationId`, `resourceId` | the saved destination, after Kingdom confirms `sessions.write` on the library (403 otherwise); an organization not declared yet is added with no projects |
| `destinations/remove` | `organizationId`, `integrationId`, `resourceId` | `removed` |
| `destinations/routes` | none | each archive (parts included) with its `partOf`, `organizations` and their destinations; nothing is sent |
| `destinations/sync` | none | one publication to every destination: `id`, `destination`, `status` (`published`, `unchanged`, `deleted`, `deferred …`, `failed …`) per archive and route |
| `routing/due` | `limit?` | sessions due for a plan, in planning order, with why |
| `routing/input` | `archiveId` | what the planner reads: the entries since the plan, their evidence, the plan so far, subagents, parent, organizations |
| `routing/record` | `archiveId`, `digest`, `through`, `key`, `by`, `proposal?` or `failure?`, `dryRun?` | `status` (`valid`, `held`, `stale`), `version`, `issues`, `notes`, the `parts` it publishes, `retired` |

`routing/plans` (`all?`, `limit?`), `routing/review` and `routing/reset` (`archiveId`) are the review queue's actions; they need no configuration. `@inixiative/archive/remote`'s `ArchiveClient` wraps these as `routingDue()`, `routingInput()`, `recordPlan()`, `routingPlans()`, `reviewPlan()` and `resetPlan()`, and `destinations()`, `libraries()`, `connectDestination()`, `removeDestination()`, `routes()` and `sync()`. The sync loop picks up changes within 30 seconds.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#routing/deletion -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Routing › Deletion (in "Archive")

##### Deletion

**Deletion.** When a re-plan drops a part from an organization, moves it, or its session is superseded, sync deletes it at that organization's destinations (a direct Archive's `delete`; Kingdom's `sessions.delete` through the paired Signet), then forgets the receipt; a part no destination still holds and no plan routes is deleted here. Any whole-session copy a destination holds is a leak (a whole session never routes) and is deleted whatever the session's plan state. Deleting a session here, or retention pruning it, retires its parts first: they are deleted at their destinations before they go here. Deleting a part retires it the same way, and its session's later plans never cut it again. Whether sync deletes anything at a destination is `cleanup` in `destinations.json` (`archive cleanup [ORG] off|leaked|all`; `leaked` or `all` for every organization needs `--all-organizations`), with per-organization overrides in `cleanupFor`. `off` (the default) deletes nothing there: no receipt deletes, no reconciliation, and pending deletes stay queued. `leaked` deletes what routing doesn't send there, keeping, with publishing off, a whole copy only when what the destination holds is a revision a plan reviewed (stripped of tool activity) and sent whole to that organization, unredacted and unpruned: it survives later captures and re-plans that keep it whole, and a copy unlike it (sent with tool activity, or of a revision no plan read) goes; `all` keeps no whole copy. Deletes run with publishing off too. `archive sync --dry-run` prints, per destination, the ids cleanup would delete under the current settings, and sends nothing. Rollout: install with publish and cleanup off (nothing new publishes), backfill so plans exist, then `archive cleanup ORG leaked`. Candidates come from this Archive's receipts, its tombstones (a session deleted or pruned here keeps the destinations that held it until each confirms the delete; a refusal stays queued), and, every ten minutes, each destination's own listing of this Archive's copies (`sourceId`), so a copy with no receipt here is found too. Another Archive's copies are never touched; through Kingdom, whose `documents.read` lists the newest documents without a source, only ids this Archive knows are taken. At most 100 deletes per destination a cycle. A part routed somewhere again is sent with `restore` (honored for parts only), so a direct destination lifts its tombstone instead of swallowing it. Deleting at a destination does not undo what was read there before. A removed destination can't be reached: its copies are deleted once it is configured again.

`archive route --backfill [--dry-run]` plans every session that has no plan yet and prints, per session, what its destinations hold now against what the plan publishes.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#connect-through-kingdom -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Connect through Kingdom (in "Archive")

#### Connect through Kingdom

Kingdom is the permission hub. Your machine's Archive talks directly only to local pieces, such as your local Foundry. It reaches a hosted Archive through Kingdom, by presenting a Signet.

First, pair this Archive with Kingdom:

```sh
bun run archive pair --kingdom https://api.your-kingdom.example --name "Work laptop" --organization your-org
```

`pair` registers this Archive with Kingdom as an **Installation**, named by a key kept in `<home>/config/kingdom/<kingdom host>/`. The same key is reused for every owner it registers with. It then asks to be registered as an integration, saying what it needs, and prints a review code with a link:

- `--organization SLUG|ID`: the organization it belongs to;
- `--library ID|NAME` (repeatable): `sessions.write` and `sessions.delete` (routing's deletes, below) on those hosted libraries. Without it, the libraries this Archive's Kingdom destinations already name, or else every hosted Archive library of the owner.

Open the link. The review opens with that owner and those libraries selected; change them if you need to, and approve. The command waits for approval, then shows which owner it was registered with and asks you to accept. Pass `--yes` to accept without the prompt; without a terminal, `--yes` is required. Only then does it collect the Signet (0600) and list the libraries it may write to. Confirming the owner protects you if someone else claimed your code into their own owner.

Next, publish an organization to one of those libraries:

```sh
bun run archive connect --kind kingdom --url https://api.your-kingdom.example --credential-file ~/.local/share/archive/config/kingdom/KINGDOM_HOST/signet-SIGNET.json --integration-id HOSTED_ARCHIVE_INTEGRATION --resource-id LIBRARY --organization-id inixiative
```

`connect` checks that the Signet grants `sessions.write` on that library before it saves anything. `serve --sync` then sends each changed session through `POST /api/v1/access/execute`. Every call carries the Signet's access token and a fresh DPoP proof (`@inixiative/signet` renews the token).

Kingdom enforces the grant on every write:

- It accepts only snapshots whose `sourceId` is this Archive's.
- It records the paired integration on the session's actor.
- It resolves a revision conflict from this source by writing over the hosted head. Older captures are still refused.

Each write is usage on the Signet. Revoke the Signet, or pause the local Archive integration in Kingdom, to stop it. `search --remote` uses `documents.search` when the Signet grants it.

Kingdom keeps no archive store. It forwards each write to the hosted Archive server, whose own token stays in Kingdom as an encrypted credential.

Foundry writes its captures to the local Archive server through `@inixiative/archive/remote`.
